title: HACD3 integrates central leptin sensitivity and peripheral thermogenesis to oppositely regulate energy balance.
abstract: The enzyme 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA-dehydratase 3 (HACD3) is involved in fatty acid synthesis, but its systemic role in metabolism is unknown. This study investigated the physiological function of HACD3 in energy homeostasis. Systemic HACD3 deficiency protected mice from diet-induced obesity by increasing energy expenditure and activating adipose thermogenesis. Conversely, deleting HACD3 specifically in leptin receptor-expressing neurons caused obesity, hyperphagia, and leptin resistance. In adipocytes, HACD3 cell-autonomously repressed thermogenesis by forming a complex with Keratin 1 (KRT1), which sequestered thermogenic transcription factors and maintained repressive chromatin. HACD3 ablation disrupted this complex, enabling nuclear translocation of PPARγ/PGC-1α and increasing transcription of thermogenic genes. In neurons, HACD3 is required for leptin receptor stability and signaling. HACD3 acts as a critical, tissue-specific regulator that simultaneously governs both sides of the energy balance equation-suppressing energy expenditure in adipose tissue while facilitating anorexigenic signaling in the brain. This dual function identifies HACD3 as a novel, multifaceted target for therapeutic intervention in metabolic disorders.

title: When fat adapts: From physiological remodeling to disease.
abstract: Adipose tissue undergoes extensive remodeling to adapt to changing physiological demands. This plasticity encompasses changes in adipocyte metabolism and number, extracellular matrix organization, vascularization, immune composition, and innervation. When coordinated, these processes preserve energy buffering, thermogenesis, endocrine function, and local tissue support. Pathological adipose tissue remodeling drives obesity-related complications and contributes to many diseases involving organ-associated adipose depots throughout the body. In cancer, tumor-associated fat can develop a metabolic and fibroinflammatory niche that promotes tumor growth and invasion, and remodeling of other depots can directly disrupt neighboring tissues. Recent studies have identified mesenchymal, immune, vascular, and adipocyte states that govern adaptive or pathological outcomes. These findings broaden therapeutic goals beyond reducing fat mass toward restoring adipogenesis, substrate turnover, thermogenic capacity, and tissue-niche function.

title: IDH2 links mitochondrial α-ketoglutarate to epigenetic thermogenic activation in brown adipose tissue.
abstract: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) regulates energy expenditure, influencing metabolic health. This study aimed to highlight the role of isocitrate dehydrogenase 2 (IDH2), a mitochondrial enzyme essential for alpha-ketoglutarate (α-KG) production, in BAT differentiation and function. In global and BAT-specific IDH2 knockout (KO) mice, cold exposure reduced thermogenesis, induced BAT whitening, and abolished the cold-dependent induction of thermogenesis by reducing the expressions of key thermogenic genes. Lower α-KG levels in IDH2 KO BAT, a key cofactor for TET2-mediated conversion of 5-methylcytosine to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine in genomic DNA, decreased the nuclear factor erythroid-2-related factor 2 (NRF2)-dependent induction of BAT-enriched lncRNA 10 (lncBATE10). Reduced induction of thermogenesis in IDH2-deficient BAT impaired energy balance. α-KG supplementation partially restored TET2 function and thermogenic gene expression in IDH2 KO mice, indicating that IDH2-dependent α-KG production is an important contributor to the thermogenic response during cold exposure. Our study uncovers a previously unrecognized novel mechanism involving the IDH2-TET2-Nrf2-lncBATE10 regulatory axis, linking mitochondrial function to epigenetic BAT regulation.

title: Multi-target phosphodiesterase inhibition overcomes adipose catecholamine resistance and ameliorates systemic lipotoxicity.
abstract: Obesity-related adipose tissue dysfunction is characterized by reduced β3-adrenergic receptor (β3AR) expression, resulting in impaired catecholamine-dependent lipolysis and limiting the efficacy of β3AR agonists. The discovery of impaired β3AR/cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling caused by concurrent β3AR downregulation (limiting cAMP production) and phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) upregulation (enhancing cAMP degradation) necessitated the development of TMDU-3 as a multi-isoform PDE inhibitor targeting PDE4, PDE1, PDE3, and PDE10. TMDU-3 robustly restored downstream cAMP-mediated phosphorylation events, including lipolytic activation, and concomitantly increased upstream β3AR expression in white adipose tissue (WAT) from obese mice. Despite a 5-fold increase in WAT mass, TMDU-3 normalized the WAT lipid composition. Moreover, TMDU-3 enhanced thermogenesis in brown adipose tissue, corrected serum accumulation of various lipids, and more effectively reduced circulating monounsaturated fatty acids than the β3AR agonist mirabegron. These findings demonstrate that multi-target PDE inhibition represents a β3AR-independent strategy superior to β3AR agonism in ameliorating obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction.

title: Platycodon grandiflorus-derived exosome-like nanovesicles drive AMPK-dependent glycolytic beige remodeling to ameliorate obesity.
abstract: Obesity is a pandemic with limited therapeutic options. Recent pharmacotherapies are constrained by tolerability, durability, accessibility, and incomplete resolution of adipose tissue dysfunction. Plant-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (ELNs) provide a natural nanoscale therapeutic platform. However, their anti-obesity effects and underlying mechanisms remain unexplored. In the present study, we investigated whether ELNs from Platycodon grandiflorus roots (P-ELNs) can mitigate obesity. P-ELNs were isolated, characterized and evaluated in high-fat diet-induced and genetic (db/db) obesity models. Analyses integrating transcriptomic profiling and metabolic flux assessment were performed to define the P-ELN-induced adipose remodeling program. Treatment with P-ELNs significantly attenuated body weight gain and reduced white adipose tissue (WAT) mass in obese mice without inducing systemic, hepatic or renal toxicity. Mechanistically, P-ELNs enhanced non-shivering thermogenesis in inguinal WAT through AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-dependent remodeling toward a glycolytic beige fat state characterized by the coordinated activation of myogenic and glycolytic gene programs. Collectively, P-ELNs represent a safe and effective nanotherapeutic strategy to combat obesity through AMPK-dependent glycolytic beige fat remodeling. Therefore, P-ELNs are a first-in-class nanotherapeutic that induce this unique beige fat subtype, providing a novel strategy to treat obesity and related metabolic disorders.

title: Growth factor VEGF-B sustains intestinal Tfh cell stemness to restrict Taurinivorans outgrowth and microbiota-driven obesity.
abstract: Autocrine signaling through vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (VEGFR-1) reprograms T cell metabolism upon TCR stimulation. We found that mice bearing conditional deletion of Flt1 (encoding VEGFR-1) in T cells developed spontaneous obesity with advancing age. Analyses of lymphoid and metabolic tissues identified a VEGFR-1+ T follicular helper (Tfh) population in Peyer's patches and mesenteric lymph nodes. Flt1 deletion impaired Tfh fitness and reduced secretory IgA in the gut, resulting in unrestricted expansion of the pathobiont Taurinivorans. Taurinivorans overgrowth depleted host taurine, which drove obesity via suppressed adipocyte lipolysis and thermogenesis. Mechanistically, a VEGFR-1-AKT signaling axis promoted Tfh cell stemness by limiting p53-mediated senescence. This Tfh-microbiota-obesity pathway was also observed in diet-induced obese mice and in humans. Oral administration of IgA reduced Taurinivorans and alleviated adiposity, highlighting the therapeutic potential of this axis. Tfh cell senescence impairs IgA production, disrupting gut microbial homeostasis, with consequences to host metabolic disease.

title: An Adipocyte MKK3-p38β Axis Preserves Insulin Responsiveness in Mice and Is Reciprocally Altered in Human Obesity.
abstract: Obesity is a major risk factor for insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes. Adipocyte stress responses can either promote metabolic dysfunction or preserve insulin action, but the contribution of the p38 MAPK activator MKK3 to adipose tissue physiology remains poorly understood. Here, we show that adipose MKK3 expression increases early during high-fat feeding and is also elevated in human obesity. In human visceral adipose tissue, MKK3 expression was positively associated with body mass index and leptin and inversely associated with HbA1c in unadjusted analyses. Using germline, Fabp4-Cre, and Adipo-Cre Mkk3-deficient mice, together with p38β-deficient mice and primary adipocytes, we found that loss of adipocyte MKK3 impairs insulin responsiveness. Adipo-Cre;Mkk3fl/fl (AdipoMkk3) mice displayed reduced insulin-stimulated glucose uptake selectively in subcutaneous white adipose tissue despite unchanged body composition and basal brown adipose tissue activity. Mechanistically, MKK3 or p38β deficiency increased p70S6K activity and inhibitory IRS1 Ser307 phosphorylation, reduced GLUT4 translocation and Akt activation, and these defects were partially rescued by rapamycin or the selective p70S6K inhibitor PF-4708671. Together, these findings identify an adipocyte MKK3-p38β-p70S6K axis that helps preserve insulin signaling during nutritional stress.

title: BMP4 as a Potential Molecular Link between Obesity and Female Fertility.
abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP4) is a member of the transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) superfamily. Accumulating evidence indicates that BMP4 is widely expressed in female reproductive tissues, including the ovary and endometrium. Therefore, this review summarizes the roles of BMP4 in regulating the physiological functions of the ovary and endometrium, including folliculogenesis, ovarian steroidogenesis, endometrial decidualization and regulation of maternal-foetal immunity. Notably, increasing studies revealed that BMP4 is also critically involved in obesity. Given the continuously rising prevalence of obesity worldwide, this review further summarizes emerging evidence on the role of BMP4 in adipogenesis, the shift between white adipose tissue (WAT) and brown adipose tissue (BAT) and metabolic dysregulation. To further elucidate the role of BMP4, we also summarize the expression patterns and potential mechanisms in reproductive disorders and obesity. We found that dysregulated BMP4 expression has been reported in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) and obesity, suggesting a potential molecular link between obesity and female fertility. Hence, the potential role of BMP4 between obesity and women's fertility is further discussed and may provide direction for further reproductive-related research. This hypothesis may guide further studies to explore the underlying mechanisms and their translational implications.

title: Dietary Sulfur Amino Acid Sensing and Metabolic Adaptation: From the GCN2-ATF4-FGF21 Axis to Transsulfuration and Redox Homeostasis.
abstract: Sulfur amino acids (SAAs), mainly methionine and cysteine, play an important role in coordinating nutrient sensing, one-carbon metabolism, redox regulation, and whole-body energy homeostasis. Dietary methionine restriction (MR) and sulfur amino acid restriction (SAAR) have gained increasing interest as nutritional interventions that produce pronounced metabolic benefits in preclinical models, including reductions in adiposity and hepatic lipid accumulation and improvements in insulin sensitivity and glucose regulation. Human intervention studies suggest biological activity and potential metabolic benefit, although the available clinical evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. These effects arise from the coordinated activation of multiple nutrient-responsive pathways. Reduced amino acid availability can stimulate the general control nonderepressible 2-eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 alpha-activating transcription factor 4 signaling pathway (GCN2-eIF2α-ATF4) integrated stress response, whereas changes in methionine-derived S-adenosylmethionine modulate mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) activity through S-adenosylmethionine sensor upstream of mTORC1 (SAMTOR)-dependent signaling. At the systemic level, hepatic fibroblast growth factor 21 contributes to the regulation of adipose tissue remodeling, energy expenditure, thermogenesis, and insulin sensitivity. At the same time, alterations in transsulfuration reshape cysteine utilization, glutathione metabolism, hydrogen sulfide signaling, and mitochondrial redox adaptation. Importantly, selective MR, broader SAAR, and total protein restriction should not be considered equivalent interventions, as their metabolic effects are influenced by cysteine availability and the degree of restriction. Nevertheless, the translation of these effects to humans remains incompletely established, and available intervention studies are limited in number, duration, and sample size. This review examines the biochemical and molecular mechanisms underlying SAA sensing and metabolic adaptation and evaluates their potential relevance to obesity, type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, with particular emphasis on future applications in precision nutrition.

title: Effect of the Long-Term Oral Consumption of Brazil Nut Oil on Adiposity and Glucose Homeostasis in MSG-Induced Obese Male and Female Rats.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Brazil nut (Bertholletia excelsa (Be)) consumption, in the form of oil or seed, has been associated with health benefits in both the lean and obese conditions; however, the influence of sex on these effects is unknown. We analyzed the effects of oral Be-oil supplementation on adiposity and glucose homeostasis in hypothalamic obese and lean male and female rodents. Methods: Male and female Wistar rats were submitted to hypothalamic lesions by monosodium glutamate (MSG; 4 g/kg). An equimolar saline solution was administered to lean, or control (CON), rats. The MSG (obese) and CON (lean) males and females were subdivided into Be-oil-supplemented (1 mL/kg; 3 times/week/8 weeks) and non-supplemented (Ns; saline) groups. Food consumption, feed efficiency ratio, body weight, and white and brown adipose tissue (WAT/BAT) content were recorded. Fasting values of glucose, triglycerides, total cholesterol, and insulin resistance (IR) were assessed. Results: MSG-obese rats presented increased adiposity, IR, and metabolic dysfunction in both sexes without altering food intake. Independently of sex, long-term oral supplementation with Be-oil did not prevent obesity development and led to reduced feed efficiency. Sex-dependent effects of Be-oil supplementation were noted, with MSGBe males showing slight improvements in glucose control and insulin responsiveness, despite worsened triglycerides and a reduction in islet number in the pancreas. In contrast, although MSGBe females presented reduced visceral WAT hypertrophy, IR worsened without alterations in insulin secretion, islet histology, or oral glucose tolerance. Conclusions: In both sexes, oral Be-oil supplementation did not prevent obesity development in MSG-hypothalamic obese rats; however, it exerted sex-dependent metabolic effects, with more positive effects on glucose homeostasis in MSG-obese males.

title: Adipose Tissue Adaptations to Chronic Kumquat Consumption in High-Fat Diet-Induced Obese Mice.
abstract: White adipose tissue dysfunction is a central event in the development of obesity-associated metabolic disorders. Kumquat (Fortunella japonica) is consumed whole, allowing intake of peel-derived bioactive compounds. Although increasing evidence suggests that kumquat exerts beneficial metabolic effects, its impact on white adipose tissue homeostasis remains poorly understood. We investigated whether chronic supplementation with lyophilized whole kumquat could attenuate adipose tissue dysfunction in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice. Male C57BL/6J mice received a standard diet, HFD, or HFD supplemented with 5% (w/w) kumquat (HFD + K) for 24 weeks. Kumquat attenuated body weight gain, reduced food intake and caloric efficiency, and decreased epididymal white adipose tissue mass. Histological analysis showed reduced adipocyte hypertrophy and a shift toward smaller adipocytes. Kumquat also decreased macrophage crown-like structures and Tnf and Il1b expression, while increasing circulating adiponectin, lowering leptin, and improving the leptin/adiponectin ratio. At the molecular level, kumquat increased Pparg, Ppargc1a, Sirt1, Cox4i1, and Ucp1 expression, together with mitochondrial DNA copy number, consistent with changes in molecular markers associated with mitochondrial remodelling and thermogenic pathways. Overall, these findings identify white adipose tissue as a relevant target of chronic whole-kumquat consumption during diet-induced obesity and suggest that preservation of adipose tissue homeostasis involves coordinated anti-inflammatory, endocrine, and mitochondrial-related molecular adaptations.

title: Imidacloprid exposure is associated with brown adipose tissue impairment in high-fat diet-fed C57BL/6 mice.
abstract: Imidacloprid, a broad-spectrum neonicotinoid insecticide widely used in agriculture, may impair mitochondria-rich brown adipose tissue (BAT), increase the risk of obesity, and alter systemic metabolic homeostasis. This study investigated the obesogenic effects of imidacloprid in a mouse model. The results revealed that imidacloprid intervention resulted in increased body weight, impaired glucose tolerance, altered lipid profiles, and a reduced mitochondrial membrane potential in brown adipocytes, particularly upon high-fat diet. Additionally, analysis using the Seahorse XF24 Analyzer also indicated a decrease in the maximum respiratory activity of BAT following imidacloprid treatment. Furthermore, integrative transcriptome analysis identified robust differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in BAT under imidacloprid treatment combined with a high-fat diet, with pathway and Gene Set Enrichment analyses revealing that metabolism-related signaling pathways (such as the thyroid hormone signaling and tricarboxylic acid cycle) were significantly affected. While future studies with expanded sample sizes and female cohorts are warranted to generalize these translational outcomes, our findings collectively demonstrate that low-dose imidacloprid exposure compromises BAT metabolic bioenergetics, highlighting its potential link to obesity as an overlooked factor.

title: Lactobacillus gasseri LG-G12 Alleviates High-Fat Diet-induced Obesity through Gut Microbiota-Bile Acid Axis.
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
abstract: The role of probiotics in weight management remains controversial. In this study, we found that Lactobacillus gasseri LG-G12 exhibits gut colonization capacity and metabolic regulation potential in vitro. In vivo, LG-G12 alleviated high-fat diet-induced weight gain and visceral fat accumulation in mice. Fecal targeted metabolomics identified bile acid metabolism as a key pathway. Furthermore, LG-G12 might exhibit bile salt hydrolase and hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activities, contributing to a bile acid profile characterized by low cholic acid and high ursodeoxycholic acid levels. Additionally, LG-G12 increased the abundance of deoxycholic acid-producing Eubacterium spp., leading to elevated DCA levels. This distinct bile acid profile activated FXR and TGR5, reducing lipid accumulation and adipocyte differentiation in the liver and epididymal adipose tissue, and promoting thermogenesis in brown adipose tissue. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that LG-G12 ameliorates high-fat diet-induced obesity via the gut microbiota-bile acid axis, positioning LG-G12 as a promising candidate for weight management.

title: Global Warming and Type 2 Diabetes: Sex and Gender as Drivers in a Multidimensional Feedback Loop.
abstract: Climate change is increasingly recognized as a determinant of metabolic health. Emerging evidence indicates that rising temperatures impair glucose homeostasis-specifically through reduced brown adipose tissue activity and increased insulin resistance-thereby exacerbating type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) risk. Concurrently, food systems drive substantial greenhouse gas emissions (GHGE), with gender-differentiated dietary patterns uniquely influencing both environmental impact and health outcomes. In this perspective, we move beyond well-established separate links to propose an original integrated and systemic conceptual framework. This framework connects gender-related drivers in dietary behaviors, GHGE, global warming, brown adipose tissue dysfunction, and T2DM risk into an integrated multidimensional feedback model, providing a novel basis to generate hypotheses for future mechanistic, epidemiological, and intervention studies, supporting gender-sensitive prevention strategies.

title: Constitutive UCP1 expression is associated with a glucose-dependent phenotype in murine mesenchymal stem cells.
abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) possess significant metabolic plasticity, enabling them to adapt dynamically to environmental stressors during tissue repair. Although UCP1 is associated with nonshivering thermogenesis in brown adipose tissue (BAT) through the uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation, its impact on MSCs metabolism remains unexplored. Herein, we evaluated the ectopic expression of UCP1 in MSCs and its effects on classical surface markers, the redox state and glucose metabolism. MSCs were genetically modified to constitutively overexpress UCP1 using a lentiviral construct. Transduction efficiency was evaluated by direct UCP1 expression and the co-expressed EGFP fluorescent tag. Surface marker phenotype and proliferation were evaluated by expression of multipotency markers and metabolic activity, respectively. Metabolic phenotypes were assessed by measuring mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), quantifying cytoplasmic and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), and evaluating glucose uptake via the 2-NBDG assay, while key glycolytic markers were evaluated by qPCR and immunoblot. UCP1-overexpressing MSCs showed a marked reduction in ΔΨm; however, normalized intracellular ATP levels remained stable across varying cell densities. Crucially, persistent UCP1 expression did not affect surface markers or cell metabolic activity, retaining their classical surface marker profile; furthermore, the engineered cells showed reduced baseline ROS levels compared with the parental line. Most notably, MSC-UCP1 cells showed increased glucose uptake and increased sensitivity to glucose deprivation, displaying increased expression of glycolytic markers. Our data indicate that constitutive UCP1 expression is associated with a shift in MSC metabolism towards a glucose-dependent state. This distinct metabolic profile highlights the plasticity of MSCs energetics and suggests a potential therapeutic application for genetically engineered MSCs in treating energy imbalance disorders such as obesity and type 2 diabetes.

title: Long-term voluntary exercise partially reverses obesity-associated transcriptomic remodeling in brown adipose tissue.
abstract: Although exercise may counteract some changes caused by obesity-induced functional and molecular remodeling of brown adipose tissue (BAT), the extent to which long-term voluntary exercise reverses obesity-associated BAT transcriptional changes remains unclear. Male C57BL/6J mice were assigned to the control, high-fat diet (HFD), or HFD plus voluntary exercise (HFD + VE) groups for four months (n = 4 per group). Interscapular BAT transcriptomic profiles were analyzed using the Clariom S Mouse Array. Differential expression was explored using eBayes ANOVA, and transcript clusters with an absolute fold change >2, a nominal P value < 0.05, and a mean log2 signal intensity ≥8 in the group with higher expression were selected for exploratory analyses. FDR-adjusted P values were additionally examined to account for multiple testing. Gene Ontology enrichment analysis was performed using DAVID. Using the prespecified exploratory criteria (absolute fold change >2, nominal P < 0.05, and mean log2 signal intensity ≥8 in the group with higher expression), 579 transcript clusters differed between the control and HFD groups. In the HFD versus HFD + VE comparison, 89 transcript clusters met these exploratory criteria; 74 showed lower expression and 15 showed higher expression with VE. None of the 89 transcript clusters remained significant at FDR <0.05 after genome-wide multiple-testing correction. GO enrichment analysis nevertheless identified coordinated immune/inflammatory and muscle contraction-related biological processes, several of which remained significant after FDR correction for GO-term testing. Long-term voluntary exercise was associated with transcriptomic changes that opposed a subset of HFD-associated alterations, particularly immune and inflammatory signatures. A restricted contractile/Ca2+-related transcriptional signature was also identified, although the transcriptomic data alone do not establish altered Ca2+ signaling. These exploratory findings highlight the need for further investigation of the cellular and signaling mechanisms underlying exercise-associated BAT remodeling.

title: CRISPR screens identify ACSL4 as a key regulator in macrophage activation and metabolic inflammation.
abstract: Pro-inflammatory macrophages drive obesity-associated metabolic inflammation. Identifying key regulators of their activation is crucial for new therapies. This study aimed to identify novel regulators of pro-inflammatory adipose tissue macrophage (ATM) activation and assess their therapeutic potential. We combined genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screening with scRNA-seq data from human adipose tissue and identified long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase 4 (ACSL4) as critical for pro-inflammatory ATM activation. Validation used myeloid-specific Acsl4 knockout mice (Acsl4fl/fl Lyz2Cre) and shRNA-mediated knockdown in macrophage cell lines (RAW264.7, THP-1, and iBMDM). Mechanisms were explored via mutagenesis, immunostaining, co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP), bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC), and transcriptional activity assays. A high-throughput screen of 8,685 DrugBank compounds was performed to identify candidates targeting ACSL4. ACSL4 deficiency markedly reduced pro-inflammatory factor expression (Tnfα, Il1β, and Il6). Myeloid ACSL4 deletion protected against high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity, correlated with reduced pro-inflammatory ATMs and enhanced adipocyte lipolysis and thermogenesis, without affecting food intake, water intake, or locomotor activity in mice. However, glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity were not significantly affected. Mechanistically, ACSL4 contributed to inflammation independent of its enzymatic/ferroptotic functions (Thr328 mutation, troglitazone insensitivity). Instead, ACSL4 translocated to the nucleus in a karyopherin β1 (KPNB1)-dependent manner. DrugBank screening identified abemaciclib as a potential inhibitor of the ACSL4-KPNB1 interaction. Notably, abemaciclib treatment reduced macrophage inflammation and attenuated HFD-induced obesity in mice. ACSL4 promotes pro-inflammatory macrophage activation through its KPNB1-dependent nuclear translocation and cooperation with IRF5. Targeting the ACSL4-KPNB1 interaction may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for metabolic inflammation.

title: Metabolic Reprogramming by Time-Restricted Feeding Confers Resistance to PM2.5-Induced Metabolic Disturbances in Adipose Tissue.
abstract: Recent research indicates that exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) not only impairs the respiratory system but also disturbs adipose tissue homeostasis, contributing to rising obesity rates and systemic metabolic disturbances. Time-restricted feeding (TRF), a dietary approach that confines daily food consumption to specific time windows, has demonstrated significant potential in preventing and managing metabolic disorders. However, it remains unclear if TRF can alleviate PM2.5-induced adipose tissue dysfunction, and the mechanisms involved require investigation. We established a PM2.5-exposed male mouse model and randomly assigned the animals to four groups: filtered air (FA), PM2.5 exposure, TRF+FA, and TRF+PM2.5. The PM2.5 and TRF+PM2.5 groups underwent whole-body PM2.5 exposure in inhalation chambers, while the remaining groups were maintained under FA conditions. Mice in the TRF+FA and TRF+PM2.5 groups were subjected to an 8-hour feeding window during the active phase (ZT16-ZT24). Our results indicated that PM2.5 exposure induced systemic energy metabolism dysregulation and obesity, characterized by reduced heat production and metabolic rate, along with adipocyte hypertrophy, lipid droplet expansion, adipokine dysregulation, and inflammatory activation in both inguinal white adipose tissue (iWAT) and brown adipose tissue (BAT). Furthermore, PM2.5 significantly suppressed thermogenesis, impaired oxidative phosphorylation, disrupted mitochondrial quality control networks, and downregulated the AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α signaling pathway. Notably, TRF intervention reactivated these signaling pathways, systematically reversed the multi-level pathological alterations, and restored mitochondrial homeostasis and energy metabolic balance. This study suggests for the first time that TRF counteracts adipose tissue dysfunction caused by PM2.5, offering a promising lifestyle intervention strategy against environment-related metabolic diseases.

title: Exploring the role of histone deacetylases and histone deacetylase inhibitors in obesity and emerging evidence from anorexia nervosa.
abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are key epigenetic regulators that modulate chromatin accessibility and transcriptional programs controlling metabolism, energy balance, and reward-related behaviors. Aberrant HDACs activity contributes to metabolic dysfunction by altering adipogenesis, thermogenic capacity, lipid profile, and hypothalamic circuits governing appetite. In obesity, specific HDAC isoforms promote adipocyte hypertrophy, impair browning of white adipose tissue, disrupt mitochondrial function, and exacerbate inflammation and insulin resistance. HDAC inhibitors (HDACi) counteract these effects by enhancing oxidative metabolism, stimulating thermogenesis, reducing adipocyte size, and improving systemic glucose and lipid homeostasis in preclinical models. Beyond peripheral metabolism, HDACi can also modulate neural pathways implicated in food intake, highlighting their potential influence in eating disorders, an area of research currently largely limited to anorexia nervosa. Research on HDACs, HDACi, and eating disorders is relatively recent; therefore, the characterization of potential molecular alterations and the identification of specific HDAC targets remain areas of ongoing development. Collectively, current evidence suggests that selective targeting of HDACs may offer a promising therapeutic strategy to correct epigenetic dysfunctions underlying both obesity and maladaptive feeding behaviors; however, translating these findings into clinical practice will require overcoming key challenges, including achieving isoform-specific selectivity, minimizing central nervous system-related side effects, and establishing efficacy and safety in human studies.

title: Dietary anthocyanins as multifunctional bioactives targeting obesity across experimental and clinical models.
abstract: Obesity has emerged as a critical global health issue, contributing to cardiometabolic and other chronic diseases. Current management strategies, including diet, lifestyle modification, and pharmacotherapy, often lack sustainable efficacy and carry side effects. The search for safe, natural interventions has drawn attention to plant-based bioactives, particularly anthocyanins, which are abundant in dark-pigmented fruits and exhibit antioxidant and anti-obesogenic effects. This review critically evaluates the anti-obesogenic potential of anthocyanins, drawing on in vitro, preclinical, and clinical studies. Preclinical evidence demonstrates that anthocyanins improve lipid and glycemic profiles and insulin sensitivity, while reducing body weight, adiposity, hepatic steatosis, and systemic inflammation. Clinical trials generally support beneficial effects of anthocyanin-rich foods and supplements on selected cardiometabolic parameters (e.g., lipids, glycemic control, and inflammation) in individuals with overweight or obesity, while effects on body weight and adiposity are modest or inconsistent. Mechanistically, anthocyanins inhibit pancreatic lipase, adipogenesis, and lipogenesis; promote fatty acid β-oxidation through AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) driven peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) signaling; enhance thermogenesis via upregulation of uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) and PR domain-containing 16 (PRDM16); and stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis in adipose tissue. In addition, anthocyanins attenuate oxidative stress and chronic inflammation by reducing reactive oxygen species, pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and by modulating nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cell (NF-κB) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways. Furthermore, anthocyanins beneficially modulate the gut microbiota, enriching species such as Akkermansia muciniphila, increasing short-chain fatty acid production, and improving intestinal barrier integrity. Overall, anthocyanins represent a compelling, multi-targeted natural intervention for obesity and its metabolic complications. These natural strategies may complement established pharmacotherapies and, when embedded in plant-forward dietary patterns and sustainable food systems, contribute to a more holistic approach to planetary health.

title: The Gut Microbiota as a Mediator of the Metabolic Benefits of Fungi and Their Polysaccharides: A Review of Evidence Addressing Causality.
abstract: Prebiotic supplementation has emerged as a promising strategy to ameliorate metabolic disorders through beneficial reshaping of the gut microbiota. Accumulating evidence suggests that fungi and their polysaccharides (e.g., those from Auricularia auricula-judae, Boletus edulis, Hirsutella sinensis, Isaria cicadae, Ramaria botrytoides, and Wolfiporia cocos) possess considerable potential in this context. The present review summarizes studies providing data relevant to the potential involvement of the gut microbiota in mediating the metabolic benefits of fungal interventions. Observed outcomes, potentially linked to the gut microbiota, included reductions in body, visceral fat, and liver weights, improved lipid and glycemic profiles, enhanced insulin sensitivity, and decreased circulating lipopolysaccharide, leptin, and proinflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6). Upregulation of tight junction proteins in the colon implied strengthened gut barrier function. Histological analyses revealed smaller adipocytes and attenuation of hepatic steatosis. Additional effects included stimulation of white adipose tissue browning and enhanced hepatic thermogenesis. Alterations in gut microbiota composition were diverse; however, a reduction in the Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio was commonly reported. Furthermore, oral administration of bacterial species enriched by fungal interventions, such as Papillibacter cinnamivorans, Parabacteroides goldsteinii, Bacteroides intestinalis, Lactobacillus johnsonii, and Enterococcus casseliflavus, reproduced the metabolic improvements, supporting their possible mediating role. Collectively, current evidence indicates that fungi and their polysaccharides may exert metabolic benefits, at least in part, through gut microbiota modulation; however, further investigation is needed to determine the extent to which the gut microbiota contributes causally to these benefits.

title: A Multi-Component High-Fibre Meal Replacement Containing Pyrus bretschneideri Rehd. Pomace Alleviates Diet-Induced Obesity by Modulating the Gut Microbiota, Bile Acid Metabolism and Hepatic AMPK Signalling.
abstract: This study employed an integrated multi-omics approach to investigate the regulatory effects and molecular mechanisms of a multi-component, high-dietary-fibre meal replacement powder containing Pyrus bretschneideri Rehd. pomace (PDMR) in high-fat-diet-induced obese mice. The results showed that PDMR significantly reduced body weight gain, Lee's index, serum lipid and inflammatory cytokine levels, and improved adipocyte morphology. Mechanistically, PDMR activated the AMPK signalling pathway, suppressed lipogenesis via the ACC-SREBP1c-FAS axis, and promoted fatty acid β-oxidation and thermogenesis through the PPARα-CPT-1 and PGC-1α/UCP-1 axes. Moreover, PDMR remodelled the gut microbiota by enriching bacteria associated with SCFA production and anti-inflammatory activity (Alloprevotella, Ruminococcaceae, Odoribacter and Prevotellaceae_Ga6A1_group) and inhibiting bacteria associated with pro-inflammatory and fat-accumulation effects (Candidatus Saccharimonas and Clostridia_UCG-014), whilst reversing the excessive accumulation of secondary bile acids. Correlation analysis established a multi-level regulatory network linking gut microbiota, secondary bile acid metabolites and AMPK target gene expression. Collectively, PDMR may ameliorate lipid metabolic disorders through a potential gut microbiota-secondary bile acid-AMPK axis, providing a scientific basis for the high-value utilisation of Pyrus bretschneideri Rehd. and the development of functional meal replacement foods.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat.
abstract: Adipose tissue has a central role in systemic energy balance and the pathogenesis of obesity and its sequelae1,2. In contrast to white adipose tissue, brown adipose tissue (BAT) uses energy to produce heat3. Detectable BAT in humans is associated with decreased prevalence of cardiometabolic diseases4. However, the complete spectrum of health conditions associated with BAT remains unknown, and high-throughput methods to quantify BAT activity in humans are lacking5,6. Here we leveraged big data and artificial intelligence to systematically define the clinical impact of BAT in a cohort of 101,243 patients from a large cancer centre. Our unbiased analyses revealed that, across all diagnoses, cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases were less prevalent in people with BAT. Using a machine learning approach, we semi-automatically quantified BAT activity in approximately 8,700 patients and demonstrated that higher BAT activity, especially in the axillary depot, is associated with lower odds of cardiometabolic diseases and healthier white fat distribution. People with BAT also exhibited more favourable glycaemic parameters, lipid profiles, inflammatory markers and echocardiographic indices. Analysis of medication usage demonstrated that angiotensin receptor blocker use was positively associated with BAT presence. As proof of concept, we showed that the angiotensin receptor blocker losartan increased brown adipocyte activity and whole-body energy expenditure. Altogether, our studies harnessing artificial intelligence and big data identify new clinical phenotypes linked to BAT and serve as a platform for drug repurposing to activate this tissue in humans.

title: An m7G tRNA-derived fragment mediated thermogenic activation of brown adipose tissue through post-transcriptional repression of Uqcr10.
abstract: Obesity, diabetes, and related metabolic disorders have become global epidemics driven mainly by an imbalance between energy intake and energy expenditure. Brown adipose tissue (BAT), the principal site of non-shivering thermogenesis, can be activated to mitigate obesity and its metabolic sequelae. RNA modification is as important regulators of obesity. The N7-methylguanosine (m7G) modification broadly influences RNA stability, enhances translational efficiency, and helps determine cell fate. However, the specific mechanisms by which m7G regulates adipose thermogenesis remain unclear. Using untargeted metabolomics, we found that cold exposure activates thermogenic metabolism in BAT and that 7-Methylguanosine is elevated in thermogenically activated BAT. METTL1-mediated m7G modification correlates positively with adipose thermogenic activation. Loss of METTL1 reduces m7G levels and impairs adipocyte thermogenic capacity. At the same time, METTL1 deficiency alters tRNA cleavage patterns and generates regulatory tRNA-derived fragments that modulate gene expression. Overexpression of tRF-Lys-CTT, which derives from an m7G-modified tRNA, inhibits brown adipocyte differentiation and thermogenic activation; conversely, inhibiting tRF-Lys-CTT produces the opposite effects. Mechanistically, tRF-Lys-CTT associates with AGO2 to form a functional RISC complex that binds the 3'UTR of Uqcr10 mRNA and directly represses Uqcr10 post-transcriptionally. Under basal conditions, elevated tRF-Lys-CTT may constrain mitochondrial function by repressing Uqcr10 expression; upon cold stimulation, downregulation of tRF-Lys-CTT relieves this repression and promotes respiratory chain supercomplex assembly and UCP1-mediated thermogenesis. In summary, our study indicates that tRF-Lys-CTT functions as a post-transcriptional regulator of metabolism that suppresses thermogenesis, and provides new insights into the regulatory relationship among the METTL1/m7G/tRF axis and thermogenic control.

title: Transgenerational effects of paternal in utero arsenic exposure on MASLD-like phenotypes.
abstract: Previous study indicated that early-life arsenic (As) exposure caused adulthood metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)-like phenotypes. This study aimed to investigate the impacts of paternal in utero As exposure on MASLD-like phenotypes in offspring. Pregnant dams received NaAsO2 (15 mg/L) through drinking water. In utero As-exposed male pups were designated as F0 mice and mated with untreated females to produce F1 offspring. F1 males were subsequently mated with untreated females to generate F2 offspring, both without further As exposure. MASLD-like phenotypes were evaluated in F1 and F2 offspring. On PNW28, As-exposed F1 offspring exhibited hepatic steatosis, glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, and obesity, accompanied by altered metabolic hormones, such as GLP-1, GIP, insulin, leptin, and ADPN. The core MASLD-like phenotypes, including hepatic steatosis, glucose intolerance and insulin resistance, exhibited transgenerational transmission from F1 to F2 generations. In F2 offspring, these metabolic abnormalities were detected at PNW45 but not at PNW28, predominantly in male offspring. In contrast, As-induced obesity and metabolic hormone alterations exhibited transgenerational attenuation. F2 offspring retained only adipocyte hypertrophy, with no significant changes in white or brown adipose tissue weight. Furthermore, hormonal alterations in F2 mice were limited to reduced GLP-1 levels in females and elevated insulin and ADPN levels in males, while other altered hormones normalized. This study is the first to confirm that paternal in utero As exposure causes MASLD-like phenotypes in F1 offspring and transgenerational transmission to F2 generation.

title: International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: diets for body weight reduction.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: The International Society of Sports Nutrition (ISSN) has developed an official position on diets for body weight reduction. This critical analysis of the literature is intended to provide a scientific foundation for practitioners, coaches, and trainees regarding the effects of the major diet types in adults who are generally healthy, physically active, and/or athletic, while drawing from clinical research in those with overweight/obesity, when relevant. This position stand does not address acute dehydration-based weight cutting, pharmacotherapy (i.e. GLP-1RAs), or bariatric surgery. The following 15 points constitute the Position Statement of the Society; the Research Committee has approved them. 1) Diets for body weight reduction can be broadly categorized by the magnitude of the energy deficit, linearity of the deficit, and macronutrient composition. These factors need to be tailored to individual preferences, tolerances, and goals.2) Very-low-energy diets (<800 kcal/day) and low-energy diets (800-1200  kcal/day) produce greater short-term weight loss but lack long-term advantages over less aggressive energy restrictions, such as calorie-controlled diets. These aggressive diets may increase lean mass loss, although adequate protein intake and resistance training may mitigate this risk. Caution is warranted about insufficiencies in vitamins, minerals, fiber, and other nutrients.3) The evidence at-large shows a lack of differential effects between intermittent fasting variants (alternate-day fasting, time-restricted eating, and twice-weekly fasting) and continuous energy restriction on anthropometric outcomes, although macronutrient quality plays an independent role in optimizing body composition and metabolic health.4) Intra-day meal frequency (as opposed to total daily nutrition) does not tend to crucially influence body weight and body fat reduction. Meal frequency may be individualized flexibly; no lower or upper limits can universally be prescribed to optimize outcomes. However, in physically active and athletic populations, distributing protein across at least three protein-rich meals (or eating occasions) per day may optimize lean mass retention and performance during sustained energy deficits.5) Resistance training and sufficient protein intake are indispensable mitigators of lean mass loss in a sustained caloric deficit, regardless of the diet type or variant. Total daily protein is of primary importance; specific distribution of the constituent doses is a secondary concern.6) For the general population, a daily protein intake of 1.2-1.6 g/kg BW is appropriate for supporting total body weight and fat loss, physical activity, and imparting benefits to musculoskeletal and cardiometabolic health.7) Daily protein intakes ranging 1.6-2.2 g/kg BW combined with resistance training may optimize muscle anabolism, while higher intakes of 1.9-3.2 g/kg BW can maximize lean mass retention in lean, resistance-trained individuals sustaining hypocaloric conditions.8) The dietary carbohydrate‒fat proportion can be individualized to personal preference for the goal of weight loss, since the range of ketogenic to low-fat diets performs similarly.9) Ketogenic diets are effective at bodyweight and body fat reduction, but they also tend to decrease fat-free mass to a greater degree than higher-carbohydrate comparators, particularly in shorter trials where glycogen and total body water shifts can influence estimates.10) Adaptations to weight loss can be physical, physiological, and/or behavioral, and converge toward reducing energy expenditure to fulfill the body's drive toward neutralizing disruptions to homeostasis imposed by the caloric deficit.11) Adaptive thermogenesis is a reduction in resting energy expenditure beyond that predicted by changes in body composition. It can occur in response to hypocaloric conditions and weight loss, but it is not an inevitable response, and it may attenuate substantially upon attainment of weight stability.12) Metabolic adaptations that reduce energy expenditure, including adaptive thermogenesis, and impair gut microbial diversity, can often be attenuated by strategic dietary and exercise programming that foster nutrient-absorption and partitioning, and metabolic flexibility.13) A multitude of tactics can be implemented to manage and overcome plateaus. However, plateaus are also opportunities/cues to practice maintaining progress made thus far (the ultimate goal is the maintenance of a plateau).14) Guidance from an interdisciplinary team of health professionals while maintaining social support is recommended for successful weight management.15) Learning how to prepare home-cooked meals (and plan meals ahead of time through the day) puts dieters in control of their nutritional fate - and in a better position to succeed in managing their body weight and body composition.

title: Cyclophilin D deficiency exacerbates diet-induced obesity and selectively enhances skeletal muscle mitochondrial respiration in male mice.
journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of obesity-associated metabolic disease, with the mitochondrial permeability transition pore serving as a key regulator of cellular energy homeostasis. Cyclophilin D, encoded by Ppif, is the principal regulatory component of this pore and has been implicated in insulin secretion, adipocyte survival, and whole-body energy balance. However, whether Ppif loss produces a consistent metabolic phenotype when challenged with high fat diet (HFD) exposure, and whether systemic metabolic alterations reflect tissue-specific changes in mitochondrial oxidative capacity, remains unresolved. Here, we characterized male, 21-weeks-old mice with germline Ppif deletion longitudinally over 34 weeks under standard (SD) and HFD using body composition analysis, indirect calorimetry, glucose and insulin tolerance testing and tissue-resolved, Seahorse-based mitochondrial respirometry. Under SD, knockout mice displayed elevated fat mass without differences in food intake or energy expenditure. High-fat feeding progressively amplified this adiposity, with knockout mice developing significantly greater body weight and fat mass than wild-type littermates by weeks 28 and 36. Glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity remained comparable between genotypes under either diet. ANCOVA revealed significant effects of lean mass (p < 0.001) and genotype (p = 0.017) on energy expenditure, as well as a significant lean mass × genotype interaction (p = 0.025). Consistent with a distinct contribution of lean mass to EE in KO vs. WT mice, we found increased ADP-stimulated mitochondrial respiration in quadriceps of knockout mice under both diets, without corresponding differences in brown adipose tissue or liver, or changes in mitochondrial content across tissues. These findings establish cyclophilin D as a diet- and tissue-specific regulator of energy homeostasis, informing therapeutic strategies targeting the permeability transition pore or cyclophilin D interactome in metabolic disease.

title: Exploring Gene Polymorphisms and Expression Patterns of Brown Adipose Tissue in Individuals with Obesity.
abstract: Adipose tissue plays a central role in energy homeostasis, influencing metabolism, thermoregulation, and overall health. White adipose tissue (WAT) primarily stores energy, while brown adipose tissue (BAT) dissipates energy through heat production. This thermogenic capacity of BAT is mediated by uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1), an important therapeutic target for obesity and related metabolic disorders. The activity and function of BAT are strongly influenced by genetic factors, including genes involved in temperature regulation, mitochondrial function, and energy metabolism. Key regulators such as uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1), Peroxisome Proliferator-Activated Receptor Gamma Coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α), PR Domain Containing 16 (PRDM16), and Cell Death-Inducing DFFA-Like Effector A (CIDEA) modulate BAT activation and energy expenditure, providing potential avenues for therapeutic intervention in obesity. Moreover, genetic variants in the Fat Mass and Obesity-Associated gene (FTO), ADRB3, and LEP highlight the links between BAT activity, lipid metabolism, and obesity susceptibility. Ethnic differences in adiposity traits, including body mass index (BMI) and waist-to-hip ratio, further emphasize the need for population-specific approaches in genetic studies. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the genetic regulation of BAT and explores their practical implications for obesity management. Importantly, we highlight gaps in understanding, such as obstacles to implementing BAT-targeted therapies, and recommend future studies that integrate genetic diversity, functional analyses, and translational research to enhance strategies for improving energy balance and metabolic health.

title: Mogroside V Promotes Brown Adipose Thermogenesis via FTO-m6A-LETMD1-UCP1 Pathway to Combat Obesity.
abstract: Obesity is a chronic, recurrent, and progressive disease caused by energy imbalance. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification regulates fat thermogenesis, potentially counteracting obesity. Mogroside V (MV) is a triterpene glycoside extracted from Siraitia grosvenorii and has shown beneficial effects in models of obesity. However, its underlying mechanism remains unknown. The objective of this study is to investigate the effects of MV on adipose thermogenesis and explore the mechanism of m6A modifications in mediating these effects. Mitochondrial respiration analysis, histological and molecular biological methods were used to investigate the thermogenesis in differentiated C3H10T1/2 brown adipocytes and adipose tissue in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mouse models, respectively. Stable cell models with overexpression or knockdown of fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) were generated to investigate the effects of FTO on m6A modification and thermogenesis in brown adipocytes. Methylated RNA immunoprecipitation-quantitative-PCR (MeRIP-qPCR) and RIP-qPCR analysis were used to reveal the potential downstream molecular targets of FTO. MV improved HFD-induced obesity and metabolic dysfunction in mice. MV also increased uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) expression in brown adipose tissue and enhanced mitochondrial respiration and expression of peroxisome proliferator activated receptor γ coactivator 1α (PGC1α) and UCP1 in differentiated C3H10T1/2 cells. Further analysis of the relevant molecular mechanisms showed that MV suppressed FTO expression, thereby increasing m6A modification of LETM1 domain-containing protein 1 (Letmd1) mRNA. The m6A-modified Letmd1 transcript was recognized by the m6A reader YTH domain-containing protein 2 (YTHDC2), thereby increasing the stability of Letmd1 mRNA. The increased Letmd1 mRNA levels were correlated with increased LETMD1 protein abundance, which subsequently enhanced the expression of PGC1α and UCP1, ultimately promoting brown adipocyte thermogenesis. MV promoted brown adipocyte thermogenesis through the FTO-m6A-LETMD1-UCP1 axis, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for obesity.

title: CNIH4 regulates systemic metabolism and exercise adaptations in male mice primarily through the modulation of β-adrenergic receptor trafficking.
abstract: Exercise improves glucose and lipid metabolism by remodeling skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, processes that depend on beta-adrenergic receptor signaling. How receptor trafficking and activation are coordinated across tissues remains unclear. Here we show that Cornichon homolog 4 controls beta-adrenergic receptor localization and activity in metabolic tissues. Cornichon homolog 4 expression increases in human and mouse skeletal muscle after resistance training. Loss of Cornichon homolog 4 in all tissues or skeletal muscle impairs beta2-adrenergic receptor trafficking and causes exercise-induced hyperglycemia and defective glucose use. Its loss also worsens diet-induced obesity. In adipose tissue, loss of Cornichon homolog 4 weakens beta3-adrenergic receptor signaling, thermogenesis and exercise-induced lipolysis. Pharmacological activation of beta2- or beta3-adrenergic receptors partially restores glucose or adipose defects. Mechanistically, Cornichon homolog 4 links adrenergic receptor signaling to extracellular matrix gene expression and Smad signaling. These findings identify Cornichon homolog 4 as a coordinator of metabolic adaptation.

title: A nuclear ERK-ATF5 axis coordinates mitochondrial metabolism and thermogenic gene expression in brown adipocytes.
abstract: Obesity and diabetes arise from disrupted energy homeostasis, underscoring the need to identify mechanisms that enhance energy expenditure. Brown adipose tissue dissipates energy through mitochondria-dependent non-shivering thermogenesis; however, the transcriptional regulators coordinating this process remain incompletely defined. Here, we investigated the role of activating transcription factor 5 in thermogenic programming and mitochondrial metabolism in brown adipocytes using in vivo and in vitro models. Cold exposure and β3-adrenergic stimulation induced activating transcription factor 5 expression in brown adipose tissue and differentiated adipocytes, accompanied by activation of thermogenic gene programs. Mechanistically, activating transcription factor 5 functioned downstream of a nuclear protein kinase A-extracellular signal-regulated kinase pathway, whose nuclear activation was required for its induction and for upregulation of uncoupling protein 1. Loss of activating transcription factor 5 impaired thermogenic gene expression, reduced mitochondrial stress response and lipolytic programs, diminished mitochondrial oxidative capacity, and suppressed fatty acid oxidation, including reduced incorporation of fatty acid-derived carbons into the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Transcriptomic analysis revealed coordinated repression of pathways related to fatty acid oxidation, oxidative phosphorylation, and thermogenesis in activating transcription factor 5-deficient adipocytes. Live-cell imaging further confirmed that β3-adrenergic stimulation selectively enhanced nuclear kinase activity, establishing a nuclear-localized signaling axis. Together, these findings identify activating transcription factor 5 as a key transcriptional regulator linking mitochondrial metabolism and thermogenic gene expression, supporting its potential as a therapeutic target for enhancing energy expenditure in metabolic disease.

title: From endocrine to immune: therapeutic potential of brown adipose tissue in remodelling the cardiovascular immune microenvironment.
abstract: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) has transcended its classical role as an energy-dissipating thermogenic organ, emerging as a pivotal endocrine and immunoregulatory hub. This review systematically delineates the novel BAT endocrine mediator-cardiovascular immune microenvironment axis. We elucidate how BAT-derived secretomes, encompassing specific batokines, lipid mediators and extracellular vesicles(EVs), orchestrate profound cross-organ crosstalk to modulate systemic cardiovascular immunity. Pathophysiological stress, including obesity and ageing, precipitates BAT whitening and dysregulates local neuro-immune-metabolic reflex arcs, thereby exacerbating atherosclerosis(AS), hypertension and heart failure. Crucially, the phenotypic transformation of perivascular adipose tissue(PVAT) is intimately linked to localized vascular inflammation and macrophage polarization. Furthermore, we critically evaluate cutting-edge pharmacological interventions targeting key pathways, including FGF21 signaling, BAT-derived exosomes, and specific lipid mediators. These therapeutic modalities span conventional adrenergic activators, advanced nanotechnological delivery systems and cell-free epigenetic therapies. By circumventing the cardiovascular toxicities of systemic sympathetic overactivation, these targeted strategies precisely remodel the adipose microenvironment. Ultimately, harnessing the profound immunometabolic plasticity of BAT unveils a groundbreaking therapeutic paradigm for combatting advanced cardiometabolic diseases.

title: A branched α-glucan from Galli Gigeriae Endothelium Corneum alleviates high-fat diet-induced obesity in a gut microbiota-dependent manner.
abstract: A highly branched α-glucan, designated GE0A, was isolated from Galli Gigeriae Endothelium Corneum and investigated for its structural characteristics, gastrointestinal fate, and metabolic effects in diet-induced obesity. GE0A had a weight-average molecular weight of 85.0 kDa and consisted exclusively of glucose. Methylation and NMR analyses revealed a branched α-glucan composed predominantly of α-(1→4)-linked glucopyranosyl sequences with O-6 branch points. During simulated digestion, GE0A remained stable in salivary and gastric phases but was partially depolymerized into lower-molecular-weight oligosaccharides during the intestinal phase. Following oral administration, Cy5-labeled GE0A-derived material remained largely confined to the gastrointestinal tract, reached the cecum and colon, and showed partial association with F4/80-positive intestinal macrophages. During in vitro fecal fermentation, GE0A-derived carbohydrates were efficiently utilized by gut microbiota, accompanied by microbial growth and increased acetate and propionate production. In high-fat diet-fed mice, oral GE0A reduced body-weight gain without altering food intake, attenuated adipose accumulation and hepatic steatosis, improved glucose and lipid homeostasis, and enhanced cold tolerance and brown-adipose UCP1 and TOMM20 expression. GE0A also alleviated systemic and tissue inflammation, oxidative stress, and PI-positive damaged cells. Antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion largely attenuated these metabolic and thermogenic benefits, whereas transplantation of microbiota from GE0A-treated donors was associated with partial recovery of several metabolic responses, supporting a microbiota-dependent mechanism. Collectively, these findings indicate that GE0A behaves as a fermentable dietary-fiber-like α-glucan that undergoes partial intestinal depolymerization and is subsequently utilized by gut microbiota to generate short-chain fatty acids associated with improved metabolic homeostasis.

title: DUSP4 activates adipocyte thermogenesis via CRTC3 dephosphorylation-dependent UCP1 expression.
abstract: Obesity arises when a chronic energy surplus overwhelms the storage capacity of adipocytes and subsequently causes systemic metabolic dysfunction. Adaptive thermogenesis, primarily mediated by uncoupling protein 1 (Ucp1) in adipocytes, serves to counteract obesity by dissipating excess energy as heat. Despite extensive studies on thermogenic regulation, the phosphatases that regulate this protective metabolic pathway remain poorly understood. Here we identify dual-specificity phosphatase 4 (Dusp4) as a critical modulator of adipocyte thermogenesis via direct modulation of CREB-regulated transcription coactivator 3 (Crtc3). Dusp4-knockout mice exhibit impaired thermogenic capacity, diminished Ucp1 expression, and increased susceptibility to diet-induced obesity coupled with severe insulin resistance. Mechanistically, Dusp4 directly dephosphorylates serine residues on Crtc3, facilitating its nuclear translocation and subsequent transcriptional activation of Ucp1. Depot-targeted restoration of catalytically active Dusp4 in inguinal adipose tissue rescues local thermogenic gene expression and reinstates Crtc3 dephosphorylation-dependent Ucp1 induction in Dusp4-knockout mice. Collectively, these findings identify Dusp4 as a key upstream phosphatase orchestrating the Crtc3-Ucp1 thermogenic axis, and highlight its potential as a therapeutic target for obesity-associated metabolic disorders.

title: Combination of Empagliflozin and Resveratrol Mitigates Hepatic Steatosis via Attenuation of Inflammation and Promotion of Adipose Tissue Browning in High-Fat Diet-Fed C57BL/6J Mice.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a major hepatic complication of obesity with a complex pathogenesis. This study aims to investigate the combined effects of empagliflozin (EMPA) and resveratrol (RSV) treatment on obesity-associated MASLD in a high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mouse model. C57BL/6J mice were fed by HFD for 23 weeks, along with treatment with EMPA (0.01% w/w), RSV (0.4% w/w), and their combination. Metabolic parameters, glucose tolerance, hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and adipose tissue morphology and function were evaluated using biochemical assays, histology, immunofluorescence, qPCR, western blotting, and 18F-FDG PET scan. Combination therapy reduced body weight gain and improved glucose tolerance more effectively than monotherapies. It significantly alleviated hepatic steatosis, as shown by decreased liver weight, triglyceride content, MASLD activity score (MAS), and serum ALT/AST levels. Co-treatment also reduced hepatic inflammation by suppressing macrophage infiltration, shifting macrophages toward an M2 anti-inflammatory phenotype, inhibiting NF-κB activation, and enhancing AMPK phosphorylation. Furthermore, the combination more effectively activated brown adipose tissue thermogenesis and induced browning in subcutaneous white adipose tissue, evidenced by upregulation of UCP1, PGC-1α, TFAM, and TMEM26, increased mitochondrial biogenesis, and enhanced cold tolerance. The combination of EMPA and RSV exerts a multi-targeted therapeutic effect against HFD-induced MASLD. This combination represents a promising novel strategy for MASLD prevention.

title: Maternal High-Fat Diet, During Preimplantation or Gestation/Lactation, Alters Mouse Offspring Metabolic, Molecular and Locomotor Phenotypes.
abstract: Maternal nutrition during offspring development influences the offspring physiology and risk of long-term chronic disease. Here, we investigate the effects of maternal high-fat diet during distinct developmental windows (preimplantation alone, EmbHFD; or throughout gestation and lactation, HFD) on adult offspring metabolic, molecular and motor behavioural outcome. Our mouse model, utilising healthy nonobese MF1 mothers, induced distinct offspring outcomes dependent upon dietary duration with some sex-specific effects. EmbHFD offspring had high serum leptin (females), elevated systolic blood pressure (SBP), low locomotory activity and diminished motor coordination. Similarly, HFD offspring not only had raised serum leptin, high SBP and poor motor coordination but also experienced excess weight gain, deficits in energy metabolism, reduced relative brown adipose tissue (BAT) mass (females) and increased muscle lipid accumulation. Transcriptomic profiling of HFD female offspring revealed upregulation of thermogenic and lipid-handling genes (e.g., Ucp1 and ApoE) in BAT alongside downregulation of mitotic regulators, suggesting impaired regenerative capacity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate, first, the risk to offspring of even transient maternal fatty diet without maternal obesity. Second, they highlight the sensitivity of periconceptional nutrition on the emergence of offspring multisystem metabolism and physiology, supporting the Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) concept.

title: Neuregulin-4 and Emerging Metabolic and Reproductive Biomarkers in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common and heterogeneous endocrine-metabolic disorder characterized by reproductive dysfunction and increased cardiometabolic risk. Conventional diagnostic criteria do not fully capture disease heterogeneity or long-term metabolic vulnerability. In recent years, multiple emerging biomarkers reflecting adipose tissue dysfunction, insulin resistance, inflammation, neuroendocrine dysregulation, skeletal muscle signaling, and gut-metabolic interactions have been investigated in PCOS. This narrative review synthesizes human studies published over the past 15 years evaluating neuregulin-4 (NRG4) and other emerging biomarkers in women with PCOS. Literature was identified through structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE and complementary databases, prioritizing observational and interventional studies using established diagnostic criteria. Evidence was critically appraised and synthesized across biomarker categories with emphasis on metabolic and reproductive relevance. NRG4, a brown adipose tissue-derived batokine, is consistently elevated in women with PCOS, particularly in those with obesity, insulin resistance, and metabolically severe phenotypes. It appears to function as a compensatory marker of metabolic stress and low-grade inflammation, with levels declining following lifestyle-induced metabolic improvement. Beyond NRG4, dysregulated adipokines, inflammatory mediators, myokines, reproductive hormones, and gut-derived metabolites demonstrate strong associations with PCOS phenotypes and cardiometabolic risk profiles. Emerging biomarkers highlight PCOS as a multisystem disorder involving coordinated metabolic and reproductive dysregulation. Integration of selected biomarkers into multimarker panels may improve phenotypic classification, risk stratification, and individualized management, although further validation and standardization are required before routine clinical use.

title: Pharmacological inhibition of CLPP stabilizes LETMD1 to boost thermogenesis and alleviate obesity.
abstract: Obesity poses a severe global health burden, and activating adipose thermogenesis offers a promising therapeutic avenue. However, the contribution of mitochondrial proteostasis to thermogenic regulation remains elusive. Here, we identify mitochondrial protease CLPP as a negative regulator of adipose thermogenesis. Pharmacological suppression of CLPP activity enhances thermogenic programmes in adipocytes. Mechanistically, CLPP interacts with LETMD1 and promotes its degradation at the post-translational level, while LETMD1 stabilization is required for the thermogenic effects induced by CLPP suppression. In vivo, pharmacological suppression of CLPP activity using hinokiflavone significantly enhances energy expenditure, attenuates weight gain, and improves insulin sensitivity in obese mice. Collectively, our study identifies a CLPP-LETMD1 regulatory axis that regulates adipose thermogenesis and highlights CLPP suppression as a potential therapeutic strategy for obesity intervention.

title: ETS-2 deficiency impairs brown adipose tissue function through Prdm16 repression.
abstract: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) and beige adipocytes regulate adaptive thermogenesis and systemic energy balance, whereas BAT dysfunction contributes to obesity and metabolic disease. Although ETS transcription factors participate in adipocyte biology, the role of ETS-2 in BAT remains unclear. Adipocyte-specific Ets-2 knockout mice were generated using the Adipoq-Cre system. BAT morphology, thermogenic responses, energy expenditure, and mitochondrial structure and function were assessed under basal conditions, cold exposure, β3-adrenergic stimulation, and mTOR activation. Primary adipocytes were used for gain- and loss-of-function analyses. RNA-seq, CUT&Tag, luciferase reporter assays, Seahorse respirometry, rescue experiments, and public human adipose single-nucleus RNA-seq analyses were performed. ETS-2 was enriched in BAT and dynamically regulated during adipocyte differentiation. Adipocyte-specific Ets-2 deletion induced BAT whitening, reduced UCP-1 expression, impaired cold tolerance and β3-adrenergic responsiveness, and decreased oxygen consumption and energy expenditure. ETS-2 deficiency also disrupted mitochondrial ultrastructure and reduced respiratory capacity in brown adipocytes. Mechanistically, integrated RNA-seq and CUT&Tag identified Prdm16 as a direct ETS-2 target. ETS-2 loss repressed PRDM16, suppressed the PRDM16-PGC-1α-UCP-1 thermogenic program, and attenuated IRS-1-PI3K/Akt-mTOR signaling. PRDM16 overexpression and mTOR activation partially rescued ETS-2-deficient phenotypes. Human single-nucleus data further supported conservation of this regulatory axis. ETS-2 is a critical transcriptional regulator of BAT thermogenic function. By directly activating Prdm16 and maintaining both the PRDM16-PGC-1α-UCP-1 axis and IRS-1-PI3K/Akt-mTOR signaling, ETS-2 preserves mitochondrial integrity and adaptive thermogenesis. These findings identify the ETS-2-PRDM16 axis as a potential therapeutic target for metabolic diseases associated with BAT dysfunction.

title: Phytochemicals and Irisin as Multi-Target Regulators of Adipose Tissue Browning and Metabolic Reprogramming: Synergies with GLP-1 Pathways.
abstract: Background: Obesity is a multifaceted metabolic disorder characterized by systemic disturbances, particularly impaired energy homeostasis, chronic low-grade inflammation, and mitochondrial dysfunction across the brain, gut, adipose tissue, and liver axes. Objectives: This review aims to examine the metabolic properties and molecular mechanisms of six key phytochemicals (berberine, resveratrol, catechins, capsaicin, thymoquinone, and phycocyanin) and the exercise-induced myokine irisin, and their roles in mitochondrial signaling and metabolic reprogramming. Sources of Evidence: A comprehensive literature search was conducted across major electronic databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus, to identify relevant mechanistic, in vivo, and in vitro studies. Results: Both the selected phytochemicals and irisin act as multi-target regulators that modulate key signaling pathways, including AMPK, PI3K/Akt/mTOR, SIRT1, Nrf2, and PPARγ. These phytochemicals and irisin can drive cell- and tissue-specific metabolic reprogramming, promoting the browning of white adipocytes, suppressing de novo lipogenesis in hepatocytes, and enhancing fatty acid oxidation in skeletal myocytes. This synergistic metabolic reprogramming enhances thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Conclusions: Co-targeting redox signaling and metabolic pathways via phytochemicals and irisin offers a powerful strategy against obesity. This integrative framework restores multi-organ homeostasis, laying the groundwork for targeted metabolic therapies.

title: An RNA thermogenic therapy to preserve lean mass and enhance metabolic health during GLP-1 weight loss.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
abstract: Current obesity therapies reduce weight but often fail to preserve lean mass or sustain metabolic benefit. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) improve obesity-associated metabolic disease, but weight loss is often accompanied by reduced energy expenditure, loss of lean mass, and rapid fat-predominant regain after treatment discontinuation. We hypothesized that pharmacologic activation of adipose thermogenesis could specifically target fat loss, complement appetite suppression by increasing energy expenditure, and improve the metabolic quality of weight loss. Guided by our finding that diet-induced thermogenesis is mediated by a zinc finger protein 423 (ZFP423)-controlled pathway, we developed adipose-directed antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) targeting ZFP423, a transcriptional repressor of brown and beige adipocyte identity. In lean and diet-induced obese mice, weekly Zfp423 ASO treatment induced white adipose beiging, increased body temperature and oxygen consumption, and improved glucose homeostasis, insulin sensitivity, lipid metabolism, mitochondrial respiration, and hepatic steatosis. When combined with the GLP1-RA semaglutide, Zfp423 ASO produced greater weight and fat loss than either monotherapy while preserving lean mass and improving metabolic outcomes. These findings identify Zfp423 as an RNA therapeutic target and support adipose thermogenesis as a complementary strategy for metabolically healthier obesity treatment.

title: Trends and Approaches in Obesity and Overweight Research Focused on White Adipose Tissue and Browning: A Bibliometric Study.
journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
abstract: The global rise in obesity has intensified scientific interest in adipose tissue biology, particularly the mechanisms underlying white adipose tissue (WAT) browning. This bibliometric study mapped the evolution, structure, and emerging directions of research on obesity, overweight, and WAT browning from 2011 to May 2025. Records were retrieved from Web of Science, Scopus, and PubMed and analyzed using VOSviewer, Bibliometrix, and Biblioshiny. A total of 2106 publications were identified, with a notable surge in output over the last decade. The United States, China, and several European countries emerged as leading contributors in terms of publication volume and citations. Influential journals were identified, highlighting interdisciplinary collaboration across molecular biology, endocrinology, and metabolic research. Keyword co-occurrence and trend-topic analyses identified thermogenesis, mitochondrial activity, transcriptional regulation, and adipocyte differentiation as central themes, whereas more recent research has shifted toward omics-based approaches, autophagy, gut microbiota, extracellular vesicles, immune regulation, and neuroendocrine pathways. Despite major mechanistic advances, the literature remains predominantly preclinical, and the contribution of beige adipocytes to whole-body energy expenditure in humans appears modest. Overall, the field has evolved from the identification of thermogenic adipocytes toward a more integrated view of adipose tissue plasticity and interorgan communication, although substantial challenges remain for clinical translation and long-term validation.

title: Metabolic Regulation of Body Size Determination by Genetic and Environmental Factors.
abstract: Body size emerges from the interplay of genetic programs and early-life environments, but the immediate executors of growth are metabolic factors. This review reframes stature as a readout of fuel allocation and cellular bioenergetics. We synthesize how endocrine drivers-Growth hormone (GH)/Insulin-like growth factor (IGF)-1, thyroid hormone, and glucocorticoids-interface with energy-sensing pathways and hepatokines to couple nutrient availability with chondrocyte matrix production, muscle protein synthesis, and bone accrual. GH promotes lipolysis and protein sparing, while IGF-1 enhances insulin sensitivity and suppresses hepatic gluconeogenesis; thyroid hormones set basal metabolic rate and thermogenesis; glucocorticoids re-partition substrates toward catabolism, prioritizing survival over linear growth. Within the developmental origins of health and disease (DOHaD) framework, fetal undernutrition and low birth weight reprogram these axes, predisposing to catch-up growth with impaired fat oxidation. We highlight actionable readouts-respiratory quotient, IGF-1/IGF-binding protein-3, leptin, and bone-formation markers-to monitor whether calories are directed to lean accretion versus adiposity. Nutritional quality, especially indispensable amino acids, functions as a metabolic signal: leucine activates mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1), arginine augments GH secretion and perfusion, and glutamine supports proliferative and redox demands.
